title: fix(models): stop catalog worker heap growth across refreshes
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repeated model-catalog preparation across plugin configuration revisions retains every previous worker generation, causing heap growth in long-running multi-agent Gateways.

## User Impact

Superseded catalog registrations can be collected while the current generation remains usable. Catalog contents, authentication behavior, source-generation checks, and stored data are unchanged. Both catalog-worker host paths request a 512 MiB V8 old-generation limit. Explicit process-wide heap flags override that limit, and native/external allocations are outside it; large real-provider working sets remain unverified. Maintainer decision: retain this selected catalog-specific budget under the explicit instruction to add a sized limit for these workers; the capacity tradeoff is accepted separately from the retention proof.

## Why This Change Was Made

Heap retainer inspection found two independent roots. The worker's cached registry loader left disposed instances in the process plugin cache. Its inline release closure also captured the request's `previous` generation, linking the current generation to every predecessor. Moving release creation to module scope and unlinking successfully disposed instances from their birth inventories removes both roots. The plugin cache owns insertion/removal bookkeeping; the instance lifecycle releases custody only after physical cleanup succeeds. Active, adopted, draining, and failed instances retain their existing ownership guarantees. The original cached loader remains in place so unchanged agents share one source graph. The worker still retains only its current prepared generation, with predecessor/successor overlap during replacement; no new catalog cache or configuration surface is introduced.

This complements #154408's generic worker idle-GC and pressure-retirement work. It does not change generic worker lifecycle code. No schema, persistence, update, or rollback changes are needed.

## Evidence

Synthetic requests go through the real worker task server and catalog preparation, alternating four plugin-config revisions. A provider fixture keeps only WeakRefs to its registration callbacks, forces collection inside the worker, and verifies an unowned collection control. The default regression uses 12 preparations; `OPENCLAW_CATALOG_HEAP_ITERATIONS=1000` enables the measured campaign.

| Measurement | Original | Fixed |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Worker heap after GC, request 100 | 95,001,232 B | 86,131,184 B |
| Worker heap after GC, request 1,000 | 178,394,488 B | 87,255,984 B |
| Growth from request 100 to 1,000 | 83.4 MB | 1.1 MB |
| Retained callbacks after replacement settles | 1,000 | 1 |

Heap is **51% lower after 1,000 preparations**. All measured catalog-entry hashes match byte-for-byte (`f066e21c211630db498310fc970e2f41d0a09f74a7ec9b29f5e5958462a05f7b`). Both controlled runs request the same 512 MiB old-generation budget, with an observed 704 MiB total V8 limit including young generation. Timings include explicit GC and are not request-latency benchmarks.

Validation uses **blacksmith-testbox**, profile **openclaw-check**, Node 24.19.0; no local suites, typechecks, or builds ran.

- Original regression: `tbx_01m316sh8rnd7wqmenkesbej0e` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35564476449)), `OPENCLAW_CATALOG_HEAP_ITERATIONS=1000 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/prepared-model-catalog-worker.heap.integration.test.ts`, using original worker blob `38c6fab786119373a0beaf22d6ebbc2aa5e3d818`: failed for the intended `1000` retained callbacks versus `1` assertion. Worker loop 18.22 s; suite 38.25 s.
- Final fixed regression: `tbx_01m31bewfj8xyck3fc8gnx5cmc` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35569932138)), same command and workload: passed. Worker loop 18.64 s; suite 38.94 s. Heap retainer paths from an isolated synthetic snapshot identified the predecessor-closure chain before the final fix.
- Focused worker and plugin suites on that final lease: **235 tests passed across 19 files**, including cached source reuse, auth, supersession, recovery, plugin adoption, inspection resources, and cleanup failures. Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/prepared-model-catalog-worker src/plugins/plugin-cache.test.ts src/plugins/plugin-instance.test.ts src/plugins/registry-lifecycle.test.ts src/plugins/registry-inspection-resources.test.ts src/plugins/loader.runtime-registry.test.ts`; wrapper wall 157.95 s.
- **Every command in the canonical changed-check plan passed** on the final lease, including core typechecking, all test graphs (817.10 s using the supported `--stripe 1/1 --concurrency 4`), lint, dead exports, schema/storage guards, import cycles, and pairing/webhook guards. The plan was generated by `createChangedCheckPlan` for the ten changed paths against base `f76d38a4ac5e5f4e6c5a5320436db169e33d5c8a` and executed with the repository's managed-command runner. It resumed at test typechecking after correcting the concurrency invocation; no check was dropped.
- `pnpm build`: **passed**, 305.2 s, including declarations, plugin runtime artifacts, CLI bootstrap checks, and Control UI bundle budgets. The same retention fixture routed to `dist/agents/prepared-model-catalog.worker.js` also **passed**, proving callback collection in the built worker (2.02 s test body, 15.10 s suite).
- The new four-case plugin-custody table was run against the original plugin owners: success disposal **failed** on the retained-instance assertion; the three failure-custody cases passed. Candidate source bytes were restored and verified afterward.
- Single-worker test costs measured during this campaign with `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`: heap fixture **22.19 s wrapper / 1.90 s test body**; custody fixture **49.65 s wrapper / 2.50 s test bodies** (includes a runtime build); plugin-cache **12.57 s wrapper / 10.96 s suite**, 35 tests passed (four new cases: 3.89 s combined, including cold failure logging). Hosted CI completed successfully in **1,223 s** (07:32:22–07:52:45 UTC); per-file hosted timings could not be retrieved because the jobs-detail request hit the account rate limit. The direct Testbox file costs above remain the measured per-file evidence.
- Hosted [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35573433437) **passed** for exact head `33da3f37cc51789ac8203d2d553018f075f131be`; no failed or pending CI jobs remain. ClawSweeper revision 2 found no blocking correctness issue and accepted the recorded catalog-specific capacity decision.
- Independent Codex autoreview: no actionable P0–P2 findings. Local changed-file formatting and `git diff --check` passed.

The intermediate inspection-owner approach was rejected: it cleared the cache Set but did not break the closure chain, and its revised form recreated unchanged runtime captures. The final fix preserves the cached loader and corrects terminal cache custody instead; the existing shared-source regression remains intact. Initial Testbox dependency hydration and repeated two-minute native checksum-sync timeouts required replacement leases. A preliminary publication-layer harness timed out; the final regression directly exercises the worker entry point. No production deployment or live-state changes were performed. The synthetic provider fixture establishes this retention defect, not that it accounts for every byte of a live Gateway's heap.

All six task-owned Testbox leases were stopped. Earlier setup runs required remote dependency installation, replacement after native sync timeouts, one optional Node resource-limit assertion correction, and three test brace fixes. These setup/fixture failures were resolved; the final source passed the selected gates.
